outcome: fear of childbirth score (Wijma Delivery Expectancy/Experience Questionnaire)
cohort: The study included 90 primigravid pregnant women aged 18-35 years, with a singleton pregnancy and gestational age of 22-30 weeks, who wished for or were doubtful about the mode of delivery, and had no clear obstacles to natural childbirth or mental disorders.
finding: Supportive group therapy significantly reduced the mean fear of childbirth score in pregnant women compared to routine pregnancy care.
mod_finding: Fear of childbirth is associated with an increased rate of elective cesarean section, and external factors like husband's opposition can compel pregnant women to undergo a cesarean section.
